transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-21 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Sam (Redwood SE), Riley (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maria Lopez, Jamal Carter, Priya Singh, Ethan Rivera

Summary (auto): Quick intro, gather success criteria for POC, go over workload numbers, discuss benchmarks and deployment requirements. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Alex from Redwood, along with Sam our solutions engineer, Riley on CS. thanks for making the time.
00:15 Dr. Maria Lopez (Aurora): thanks Alex, yeah excited we cut the pre-read. quick intro from our side — I'm Maria, lead on ML for patient triage. Jamal is our CTO and Priya handles security.
00:28 Jamal Carter (Aurora): morning all, we want to scope a POC to validate the triage assistant end-to-end — both quality and infra fit.
00:40 Sam (Redwood): great, can you walk through your success criteria first? that helps orient whether hosted/dedicated/private is right.
00:50 Dr. Maria Lopez: sure — three things: 1) model quality — F1 on our labeled triage dataset should be within 3 points of our on-prem baseline, 2) latency — for short triage responses < 2 sentences we need p95 < 400ms ideally, and 3) security/compliance — PHI must not be stored offsite, and audit logs are required.
01:20 Priya Singh: to add — we need KMS integration for encryption, SSO via SAML, and evidence of SOC2 + HIPAA. if hosted, we need a BAA.
01:35 Alex: understood. those are common asks. Hosted can be accelerated for time-to-value but typically Dedicated or Private are chosen when PHI retention and strict network controls are required.
01:50 Sam: quick question on workload sizing — what's your expected QPS and traffic profile?
02:00 Dr. Maria Lopez: average daytime QPS around 20, with peaks up to ~120 during morning surges. Typical request sizes are short — 30-80 tokens user prompts, responses 40-120 tokens. We also will do batched inference for runbook generation sometimes — longer sequences up to 1024 tokens but lower frequency.
02:25 Ethan Rivera: infrastructure note — we prefer starting single region US-west, but need data residency in US only. also would like ability for VPC peering for private deployments.
02:40 Sam: ok that's helpful. from Redwood's side, for these numbers hosted easily supports this profile; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput for the peak bursts, and Private (on-prem or VPC private control plane) gives you full control for PHI.
03:05 Jamal: baseline cost is important — can you ballpark cost differences?
03:12 Alex: rough guidance: hosted lowest time-to-value and lowest ops for you; Dedicated medium cost but predictable unit economics; Private highest engineering overhead but necessary sometimes for HIPAA with no egress. we'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
03:35 Sam: on benchmarks — we propose running a 2-hour benchmark with your sample corpus: 1) single-request tail latency profile (p50/p95/p99), 2) throughput run at 120 QPS sustained for 15m to check autoscaling and queues, 3) quality metric evaluation vs your labels.
04:00 Dr. Maria Lopez: sounds good. we also want reproducible runs and CSV outputs for comparison.
04:10 Alex: absolutely, Sam will prepare the harness. question on model — are you planning to use a fine-tuned private model or open model?
04:22 Dr. Maria Lopez: we have an internally fine-tuned LLM on clinical notes; we'd prefer to test with that. we may also compare to a Redwood curated open clinical model.
04:40 Sam: ok for a bring-your-own-model scenario we have two options: hosted with encrypted model artifacts (if allowed) or Dedicated/Private where you keep the model artifacts inside your VPC. for fine-tuned weights with PHI, most customers go Dedicated with VPC peering or Private if regulatory controls require no egress.
05:10 Priya: clarification — does Dedicated allow us to manage keys? we need customer-managed keys (CMK).
05:20 Alex: Dedicated supports KMS integration and customer-managed keys for data at rest. Private supports HSM and full key control. Hosted supports KMS but may not meet all enterprise-only HSM requirements.
05:40 Ethan: network wise — can we do private networking for Dedicated? VPC peering?
05:45 Sam: yes Dedicated offers VPC peering and NAT egress control. Private gives you a private control plane, and on-prem can be fully air-gapped.
06:00 Jamal: about latency SLOs — you said earlier 400ms p95, can Redwood meet that for our 120 QPS burst?
06:10 Sam: depends on model size and selected hardware. for smaller optimized models we can hit ~200-300ms p95 for short responses on A100/A10G pools with appropriate batching disabled for tail-sensitive calls. for larger models or long context, expect higher latencies. part of the POC benchmark will surface exact numbers.
06:40 Dr. Maria Lopez: model size — our fine-tuned is 30B parameters. do you support quantization?
06:48 Sam: yes we support quantized paths and kernel selection in the runtime. quantization can reduce latency and cost but we need to validate quality on your labels.
07:05 Alex: question on data retention — what's Aurora comfortable with for logs and request-level retention?
07:12 Priya: we require request logs for debugging but must redact PHI; audit logs must be retained 7 years per our policy. if hosted, we would need explicit retention controls and BAA clauses.
07:30 Alex: understood. Redwood Console provides per-route retention controls and audit logs; we can configure redaction and retention periods, but for 7-year retention with PHI you may want Dedicated or Private to satisfy legal controls.
08:00 Jamal: who will run the benchmark and where will it run?
08:05 Sam: Redwood will run the benchmark against the deployment of choice. we usually offer two benchmark modes: 1) hosted ephemeral run (fast) and 2) dedicated/private where we coordinate with your infra team to run inside your VPC or peered network. for BYO-model we'll need artifact access — ideally via secure staging bucket or direct pull inside your VPC.
08:35 Ethan: we can provide a staging S3 with limited access for the run and temporary credentials.
08:40 Sam: perfect. timeline — what's your desired POC timeline?
08:45 Dr. Maria Lopez: target is a decision in 6 weeks. 2 weeks for setup and benchmarks, 2 weeks for evaluation/fixes, 2 weeks for internal approvals.
09:00 Alex: that's reasonable. we can aim for kickoff next Mon, benchmark next Tue-Wed, report by end of week.
09:10 Priya: security review will need SOC2 Type II and penetration test reports. also we may request code access for agents that interact with EHR APIs.
09:25 Alex: we can share redacted SOC2 report and a summary of penetration testing. for deeper requests we'll follow our legal process.
09:40 Sam: technical deep-dive question: for your longer batch runs (1024 tokens) do you expect them to be synchronous? or can they be async?
09:50 Dr. Maria Lopez: mostly async for runbook generation, so latency is less critical there. the critical path is triage which must be low-latency and highly available.
10:05 Alex: ok. for low-latency triage we recommend a smaller optimized model variant pinned in Dedicated for the peak path, and longer generation on a larger model in a warm fallback pool. that tradeoff keeps p95 low while preserving quality for complex cases.
10:35 Jamal: curious — how does Redwood handle graceful degradation if capacity spikes beyond Dedicated pool?
10:42 Sam: routing policies — automatic fallback to a cheaper variant or to a hosted instance in another region if you permit, plus queueing/backpressure controls and rate-limiting. we can configure canary rollouts and circuit-breakers.
11:05 Priya: auditability — does your logging include token-level cost breakdowns? we need to show unit economics in procurement.
11:12 Riley (CSM): yes, Console shows token-level cost, per-route dashboards and latency breakdowns; we can share sample reports.
11:25 Dr. Maria Lopez: any limitations around fine-tuning in hosted mode? we have proprietary corpora.
11:30 Sam: hosted allows fine-tuning in a managed flow, but artifacts may be stored in managed buckets depending on contract. for proprietary corpora and PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private so artifacts live in your environment.
12:00 Jamal: ok to recap our decision criteria? Maria can start.
12:05 Dr. Maria Lopez: decision hinges on 1) PHI constraint — if we cannot accept any third-party storage of model artifacts/data then Private; 2) latency — if p95 < 400ms at peaks we can accept Dedicated; 3) cost and speed to deploy — Hosted preferred for speed if security is ok; 4) ease of operations — Dedicated reduces our ops burden vs full Private.
12:35 Alex: good summary. sounds like Aurora will test Hosted first for speed, but leaning Dedicated for production if benchmarks and contractual terms for KMS and BAA line up.
12:50 Jamal: yes we want to see numbers.
13:00 Sam: next steps — we'll: 1) send POC SOW + pricing for hosted/dedicated/private, 2) prepare benchmark harness and schedule run, 3) share SOC2 + HIPAA summary and network guide.
13:20 Alex: action owners and dates captured. anything else?
13:30 Priya: please include specifics on key management (CMK/HSM) and data residency controls in SOW.
13:40 Ethan: I'll send VPC peering details and a staging S3 path by end of week.
13:50 Riley: I'll set up the calendar invite for the benchmark run and include test corpus instructions.
14:05 Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with materials.
14:15 Dr. Maria Lopez: thanks, talk soon.

-- End transcript --

Notes on transcript quality: auto captions had a few mislabels (speaker numbers) and occasional swapped acronyms. timestamps approximate.

Benchmark plan (brief):
- Run A: Hosted quick-run using Redwood managed model (validate p50/p95/p99 latencies for short prompts)
- Run B: Dedicated pool run with BYO 30B model to measure p95 at 120 QPS and validate autoscale behavior
- Run C: Private (if required) run inside Aurora VPC to validate KMS/HSM, egress controls and long-term retention behavior

Success criteria (explicit):
- Quality: F1 within 3 points of on-prem baseline on labeled triage dataset
- Latency: p95 < 400ms for short triage responses at 120 QPS peak
- Security: KMS integration and BAA in place; SSO/SAML + RBAC; audit logs enabled and retention controls available
- Ops: reproducible benchmark CSVs; documentation for deployment and rollback; SOW signed
